meta.title: Article bank and house style — the feed into the design prompt
meta.purpose: Working titles and house-style rules for the next version of Crisp & Counter. This is the raw material a designer or writer receives before touching a page: what to write about, what it must never say, and how organic traffic is legitimately earned.
meta.status_rule: Every title below is a working title and an editorial hypothesis. None is a claim about popularity, search volume, trend data or product superiority — no keyword tool was consulted and no demand estimate is made. Titles are shaped like the questions buyers actually type; whether anyone types them is answered only by the Search Console query report after it exists (S-03, Q-07).
meta.how_to_use: Pick topics only after the measurement path is chosen (suggestions: PATH-C). Each topic names the evidence required before it is written; a topic whose evidence cannot be obtained is rewritten as a checklist of questions, or not written. Published guides go into tools/content.py GUIDES, which feeds the sitemap and RSS feed automatically.
meta.counts: 14 working titles in 5 clusters · 6 map to published guides · 8 are proposals · 10 house-style rules · 1 organic-traffic loop
meta.id_note: T-01..T-16 are the brief's hypothesis rows published in the earlier design pack (arena/76128338-affil1 lineage); T-17..T-30 are this session's additions. One id space, one bank.

style_rules.rule: Never claim a test that did not happen. No first-person past-tense claims of cooking, measuring, buying or lab work anywhere — not even as a hypothetical example.
style_rules.basis: FTC Endorsement Guides FAQ: endorsements must reflect the honest opinion of the endorser and cannot be misleading. Official: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking (retrieved 2026-11-20).

style_rules.rule: No superlatives or rankings without evidence: no claim of being the finest, the first, the top-rated, the award-winner or the leader of any list.
style_rules.basis: Associates Program Policies, Links on Your Site: "You must not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product, an Amazon Site, or any of our policies, promotions, or prices." Official: https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/policies (retrieved 2026-11-20).

style_rules.rule: No price, star rating, review count or stock figure anywhere on the site. Send the reader to Amazon, where the numbers are current.
style_rules.basis: Associates Program Policies: prices and availability may be shown only where Amazon serves the link carrying them, or where data arrives via Creators API or PA API. Neither is connected here. Official: https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/policies (retrieved 2026-11-20).

style_rules.rule: No hollow meta: never write "in this article", "look no further", "we've got you covered", "game-changer", or a paragraph that promises to tell the reader what the next paragraph tells them.
style_rules.basis: Design decision. It is the single loudest register of generated text.

style_rules.rule: Every factual product claim carries a source link to the listing or an official document, or is left blank and flagged. Blanks are honest; filled-in guesses are not.
Write one concrete scenario per card or section — the 6pm frozen-chips panic, the counter with 40 cm of clearance, the six-person Sunday dinner. Specific scenes beat adjectives.
style_rules.basis: Design decision. It is also the cheapest way to read like a person who has a kitchen.

style_rules.rule: Titles answer a question or promise a concrete artefact (chart, checklist, audit). No adjective-stack titles.
style_rules.basis: Design decision. Question-shaped titles match how buyers search and how the existing guides are structured.

style_rules.rule: Read every page aloud before shipping. If two sentences in a row have the same rhythm, rewrite one.
style_rules.basis: Design decision. Monotone rhythm is the second-loudest register of generated text.

style_rules.rule: The disclosure strip sits under the masthead on every page and repeats in the footer, carrying the required sentence verbatim: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."
style_rules.basis: Associates Program Operating Agreement §5 (retrieved 2026-11-20): "You must clearly and prominently state the following … 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.'" Official: https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/agreement

style_rules.rule: Illustrations are labelled as illustrations and never posed as photographs of a test. Product photographs replace them only when real photos of the exact variant exist.
style_rules.basis: FTC honesty principle above; repository image policy (review/images.html).

traffic_plan.principle: Organic traffic is earned by one indexable site that answers real questions and can prove it. The loop is publish → sitemap and RSS → internal link → measure queries → choose the next topic from the measured ones. Nothing in the loop guesses demand.
already_done: One canonical site — no competing edition is indexable (archive/ is noindex; robots.txt blocks it).
Sitemap and RSS feed regenerated from the same data as the pages, so no published guide is missing from either.
Canonical URLs, Open Graph images and Article/FAQPage/BreadcrumbList structured data on generated pages.
Question-shaped guides in deliberate clusters, each linking to its cluster peers and to the product pages.
A disclosure strip and a per-link sponsored mark on every page, so a search engine never has to guess the relationship.
missing_and_gated: Search Console property and sitemap submission (S-03) — needs the owner's Google account. Until it exists, every topic choice is an editorial hypothesis (Q-07).
28-day query review against the previous window (S-07 gate) — needs the report, not instinct.
A root domain instead of the repository subpath (S-11) — a brand and budget decision (Q-17).
Any paid acquisition — refused as policy (S-21), recorded so it is not rediscovered as an idea.

topics.working_title: Air Fryer Times and Temperatures: A Cheat Sheet for the Foods You Actually Cook
topics.search_intent: informational — the reader owns an air fryer and wants a printable answer
topics.why_on_the_list: A chart is the most linked artefact a small publication can make, and it earns attention from owners, not only buyers.
topics.evidence_before_writing: USDA FSIS safe-minimum-temperature chart for the doneness column (official); cooking times only as "as stated by the manufacturer" per listing, or left blank. Do not invent times.
topics.maps_to: new guide — feeds the thermometer cluster

topics.working_title: Foil, Parchment, or Oil Spray: What an Air Fryer Basket Will Actually Tolerate
topics.search_intent: informational with a safety undertone — the reader is about to do something and wants permission or a warning
topics.why_on_the_list: Care questions arrive before buying questions and are answerable from manuals rather than testing.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Manufacturer care instructions for each of the three fryers; where a manual is not obtainable, publish the question list, not rules.
topics.maps_to: new guide — pairs with the cleanup guide

topics.working_title: Basket or Oven-Style Air Fryer: The Five Questions That Decide It
topics.search_intent: commercial investigation — the reader is choosing between two shapes
topics.why_on_the_list: The format choice is the first fork every buyer meets; the site already carries the guide.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Published — exists and closes with what it does not claim.

topics.working_title: Combined Quarts Lie: Dual-Basket Math for Real Meals
topics.search_intent: commercial investigation — the reader suspects a spec is doing marketing work
topics.why_on_the_list: It turns a spec sheet into a kitchen argument, which is what a buyer is actually having with themselves.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Published — basket volumes quoted only as the listing states them.

topics.working_title: The Counter-Space Audit: Measure Once Before You Buy Any Air Fryer
topics.search_intent: informational — the reader has been burned by a too-big appliance before
topics.why_on_the_list: Fit is the most common return reason an owner can actually prevent with a tape measure.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Published — dimensions quoted only where a listing states them; the audit itself is measurement advice, not specs.

topics.working_title: How to Clean an Air Fryer Basket Without Wrecking the Coating
topics.search_intent: informational — owner-stage, arrives weeks after purchase and links back to the buying guides
topics.why_on_the_list: Owner-stage questions build the returning audience that later trusts the buying guides.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Manufacturer care instructions per model; no cleaning chemistry claims without a source.
topics.maps_to: new guide — deepens the cleanup cluster

topics.working_title: New-Appliance Smell After the First Use: Off-Gassing, Residue, or a Real Problem?
topics.why_on_the_list: A recurring worry-shaped query class; answering it calmly is exactly the publication's register.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Hold until manufacturer guidance or a public-health source can be cited. Without one, do not write it — a guessed safety answer is the one thing this site cannot ship.

topics.working_title: Do You Need a Meat Thermometer for an Air Fryer?
topics.search_intent: informational sitting on a purchase — the reader is one answer away from a basket add
topics.why_on_the_list: It is the bridge between the two product clusters, and the site already carries the guide.

topics.working_title: Instant-Read or Leave-In: Which Probe Saves Which Dinner
topics.search_intent: commercial investigation — the reader will buy one of the two this week
topics.why_on_the_list: The two thermometer rows are the easiest honest comparison on the site, because the difference is use-scenario, not quality.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Listing-stated features (probe count, stated response time) with source links; no accuracy claims beyond what the listing states.

topics.working_title: Internal Temperature Chart: The One Page That Ends the Guessing
topics.season: evergreen, with a holiday spike the site should not need to shout about
topics.why_on_the_list: The strongest organic-traffic artefact in the cluster, and every figure can carry an official source.
topics.evidence_before_writing: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature chart, quoted with its official URL and retrieval date (closes FLG-012 if adopted).

topics.working_title: Thanksgiving When the Oven Is Full: The Countertop Overflow Plan
topics.search_intent: seasonal planning — the reader is hosting and the oven is the bottleneck
topics.why_on_the_list: Seasonal features are the one place a small site can be early instead of big; the two holiday guides already carry the argument.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Published — capacity stated only as listings state it.

topics.working_title: The 6pm Frozen Reset: Air Fryer Math for Weeknights
topics.search_intent: informational-to-commercial — the reader wants tonight solved, then notices the format question
topics.why_on_the_list: The weeknight scenario is the voice the front page already uses; it earns the click the guide can convert to a format decision.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Listing-stated presets and capacities only; frozen-food times as "as the listing states", or blank.

topics.working_title: Meal Prep Sunday: What an Air Fryer Changes and What It Doesn't
topics.search_intent: informational — a habit question with a format answer hiding inside
topics.why_on_the_list: Habit content is the returning-reader engine; the guide already exists in the build.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Published — capacity scenarios, not cooking claims.

topics.working_title: The Small Gift That Fixes Overcooked Dinners
topics.search_intent: commercial — a gift buyer with a budget and no domain knowledge
topics.why_on_the_list: The thermometer cluster is gift-priced and giftable without any quality claim, because the article sells the problem, not the brand.
topics.evidence_before_writing: Listing-stated features and packaging claims only; no price, no "under $X" framing — price display is prohibited without a feed (ST-19).
